scenario_premise_subsections.1.1:
1.1 Setting
Naval Support Activity Amber Reach (NSA AMBER REACH) is a forward naval installation on Talaveras Island, in the territorial waters of the Republic of Sundara, a treaty partner. The installation supports rotational surface forces operating in the eastern approaches to the Verrick Strait.
Relations with the Rhoan Federation have deteriorated over the preceding six months following repeated unsafe intercepts of Sundaran-flagged merchant traffic in the strait. No state of armed conflict exists. The installation has been at Force Protection Condition BRAVO for twenty-six days.
scenario_premise_subsections.1.2:
1.2 The deploying unit
Surface Action Group SENTINEL (SAG SENTINEL) is scheduled to depart NSA Amber Reach at 0530K, 4 September, to execute Operation TIDEWALL rotation 26-04 — the escort of Sundaran-flagged commercial shipping through the eastern approaches to the Verrick Strait.
USS BRENNAN (DDG 129) — flagship
USS ASHFORD (DDG 133)
USS KETTLEWELL (FFG 68)
USNS PALO DUNE (T-AKE 15)
Approximately 1,150 personnel. Rotation 26-04 is programmed as a nine-day rotation. No intermediate port call is scheduled and the group is programmed to return to Amber Reach on completion of the rotation. The operation's route, timing, and escort geometry are restricted.
scenario_premise_subsections.1.3:
1.3 The facility
Building 14, the Communications Security Material Facility (CSMF), houses the installation's communications security material and the equipment used to prepare it for issue, including KL-9 key transfer devices, which are stored in sealed security containers when not being actively prepared for issue. The most sensitive space in Building 14 is the Secure Communications Material Vault, which sits inside Restricted Area ZONE-3.
Two sections work in Building 14 and their records do not overlap. The Communications Security Material Custodian holds the container inventory, the issue plan, and the issue and receipt records: what was drawn, by whom, to which unit, and in what condition. The COMSEC Equipment Maintenance Section, in the Building 14 maintenance bay, holds equipment maintenance records, vendor product advisories, configuration status, and the service-life record for device components. Neither section holds the other's records, and neither holds unit movement or operating schedules.
scenario_premise_subsections.1.4:
1.4 The watch
During the mid watch of 3-4 September, several apparently minor irregularities are reported to the Base Defense Operations Center (BDOC) by different departments while SAG SENTINEL completes its pre-sail preparations. No single department has visibility across all of them. No report describes an intrusion, a compromise, a missing item, or an unaccounted person.
The Installation Watch Officer (IWO) must decide how the night's traffic is dispositioned before turnover.
scenario_premise_subsections.1.5:
1.5 The decision
The IWO selects exactly one of:
NOTIFY_IMMEDIATELY — wake the Command Duty Officer for immediate notification of the Commanding Officer under ARI 5510.7B.
REQUEST_MORE_INFORMATION — one clarification round.
INCLUDE_IN_ROUTINE_UPDATE — hold for the 0600 watch turnover brief.
The question before the IWO is not whether harm has occurred or been proven. It is whether the available evidence constitutes an unresolved anomaly that may affect a unit scheduled to deploy within twelve hours.

E01.notification_standard:
AMBER REACH INSTRUCTION 5510.7B
IMMEDIATE NOTIFICATION STANDARD
Naval Support Activity Amber Reach

Ref: (a) ARI 2280.1A, Communications Security Material Incident Reporting
     (b) ARI 3120.4, Installation Watch Organization and Turnover

1. PURPOSE. To establish the conditions under which the Installation Watch Officer shall notify the Command Duty Officer immediately, vice holding a matter for routine watch turnover.
2. IMMEDIATE NOTIFICATION CRITERIA. The Command Duty Officer shall be notified immediately when any one of the following applies.
Criterion A — Corroborated restricted-area intrusion. Two or more independent indicators of possible unauthorized access to a Controlled or Restricted Area exist, and the indicators cannot be fully explained or resolved during the current watch. Independent indicators include, but are not limited to: use of an unauthorized, expired, or revoked credential; physical observation of an unidentified person; unexplained loss or degradation of surveillance coverage; door, container, or seal irregularities; and authentication to an internal system associated with an unauthorized identity.
Criterion B — Possible communications security compromise. Credible evidence exists that an unauthorized person may have accessed, handled, connected to, altered, or obtained records concerning cryptographic equipment or restricted communications material. Confirmed theft, confirmed data loss, or confirmed modification is not required.
Criterion C — Unresolved risk to an imminent operation. An unresolved security anomaly may affect communications, force protection, or mission integrity for a unit scheduled to deploy within twelve hours.
3. ROUTINE UPDATE STANDARD. A matter may be held for routine watch turnover only when all of the following are true:
a. It is limited to a single administrative or technical irregularity. b. No independent corroborating indicator exists. c. The likely cause has been identified. d. No protected equipment or restricted communications material is credibly implicated. e. No imminent operation could be affected.
4. STANDARD OF JUDGMENT. Where evidence is incomplete, personnel shall classify the matter according to plausible operational risk, not according to what has already been conclusively proven. The absence of confirmation is not evidence of absence.
5. CLARIFICATION. The IWO may direct one round of clarification prior to decision. Clarification shall not be used to defer a decision that the criteria in paragraph 2 already require.

reports.reported_status: Closed. Cause identified and corrected. No indication of attempted penetration.

SERIAL:     NSAAR-PSD-0463
PRECEDENCE: ROUTINE
DTG:        032311K SEP 26
FROM:       Physical Security Division, Perimeter Watch
TO:         Installation Watch Officer, BDOC, NSA AMBER REACH
INFO:       Security Department Duty Chief
SUBJ:       PERIMETER INTRUSION DETECTION ACTIVATION, SECTOR 4
REF:        (a) ARI 5510.7B

1. SITUATION. At 2258K the perimeter intrusion detection system generated a Zone 4-B activation on the seaward fence line south of Tower 2.
2. DETAILS. Reaction force arrived on scene at 2303K and walked the affected fence panels and the adjacent clear zone under lights. Fence fabric, outriggers, and tension wire intact. No cut, climb, or lift signature. No footprints in the graded strip. Tower 2 reports no observation of movement inside or outside the clear zone during the period.
3. ASSESSMENT. Activation is attributed to spray-driven salt accumulation shorting the sensor cable termination at post 4-19 during the onshore gusts recorded between 2230K and 2255K. Zone 4-B has recorded five weather-attributed activations in the past forty days, all similarly adjudicated, and the termination at post 4-19 accounts for three of them.
4. ACTIONS TAKEN. Termination cleaned, dried, and re-sealed. Zone reset and functionally tested end to end at 2306K. Sector 4 restored to full detection. Corrosion work order PWD-7801 opened against post 4-19.
5. STATUS. Closed. Cause identified and corrected. No indication of attempted penetration.
6. POC. MA1 R. Tomasek, Perimeter Watch Supervisor, x4412.

PRECEDENCE: ROUTINE
DTG:        040141K SEP 26
FROM:       COMSEC Equipment Maintenance Section, Building 14
TO:         Installation Watch Officer, BDOC, NSA AMBER REACH
INFO:       Building 14 Facility Manager; Regional Technical Support Activity
SUBJ:       SERVICE-LIFE REPLACEMENT AVAILABILITY NOT EXECUTED, KRC-2 CELLS,
            PRODUCTION LOT 27-D
REF:        (a) ARI 2280.1A
            (b) Caldera Integrated Systems Product Advisory CIS-PA-26-047

1. SITUATION. The availability of 1-2 September, at which the KRC-2 cells fitted in KL-9 key transfer devices of production lot 27-D were to be replaced, was not executed. This section reports the carry-over for watch awareness.
2. DETAILS. Reference (b) fixes the certified service life of KRC-2 cells fitted in production lot 27-D at 0001Z, 7 September 2026. Sixteen lot 27-D devices are carried on the installation's configuration record. Cell replacement requires the device to be opened at a certified maintenance activity by the regional technical representative. The representative's travel to Amber Reach was cancelled on 31 August when his prior tasking overran, and the availability has been rescheduled to 9-10 September. Replacement cells for all sixteen devices are on hand in Building 14 and have been inventoried against the requirement.
3. EQUIPMENT. The KRC-2 cell is the internal power source of a KL-9 key transfer device. It maintains the device's loaded key material and its tamper-response circuit between uses. No lot 27-D device has reported a cell fault and every lot 27-D device has passed each scheduled functional test.
4. SCOPE OF THIS REPORT. This section holds equipment maintenance records, vendor product advisories, configuration status, and the service-life record for device components. It does not hold the container inventory, the issue plan, or issue and receipt records, and it therefore cannot state which devices have been drawn, to whom any device has been issued, or where any device now is. It holds no unit movement or operating schedule. No assessment of operational impact is offered, and none can be made from the records this section holds.
5. ASSESSMENT. Routine service-life maintenance action carried past its scheduled availability. Availabilities of this kind slip three or four times a year, most often on technical representative travel, and are worked at the next scheduled date. The cells are on hand and the work is scheduled.
6. ACTIONS TAKEN. Availability rescheduled to 9-10 September and confirmed with the Regional Technical Support Activity. Cell stock inventoried and reserved against the requirement. Advisory CIS-PA-26-047 left open in the maintenance record pending execution.
7. STATUS. Open. Lot 27-D cell replacement carried to the availability of 9-10 September.
8. POC. CTM1 P. Gundersen, COMSEC Equipment Maintenance Section, x4471.

1. SITUATION. This cell has consolidated the equipment maintenance record and the pre-sail issue record for the KL-9 key transfer devices issued to SAG SENTINEL for Operation TIDEWALL rotation 26-04. Six devices of production lot 27-D are aboard the four units of the group. The certified service life of the KRC-2 cells fitted in that lot ends at 0001Z, 7 September. The group departs at 0530K, 4 September on a nine-day rotation and is programmed to return to Amber Reach on 13 September.
2. EQUIPMENT. The KRC-2 cell is the internal power source of a KL-9 key transfer device. It is what maintains the device's loaded key material and its tamper-response circuit between uses. Reference (c) fixes the certified service life of KRC-2 cells fitted in production lot 27-D at 0001Z, 7 September 2026. Cell replacement requires the device to be opened at a certified maintenance activity by the regional technical representative; it cannot be performed by a unit or by the custodian.
3. ISSUE. Devices KTD-812, KTD-815, KTD-819, KTD-823, KTD-826, and KTD-831 — all production lot 27-D — were drawn from Container C-7 against issue plan TIDEWALL 26-04 and issued between 0145K and 0212K, 4 September: three to USS BRENNAN and one each to USS ASHFORD, USS KETTLEWELL, and USNS PALO DUNE. Receipts are dual-signed, container seals and inventory reconcile, nothing is unaccounted for, and every device passed its startup self-test at issue. No person outside the appointed chain handled any device at any point.
4. MAINTENANCE STATUS. Replacement of the lot 27-D cells was scheduled for the availability of 1-2 September. The regional technical representative's travel was cancelled on 31 August and the availability was not executed. It is rescheduled to 9-10 September. Replacement cells for all sixteen lot 27-D devices held at Amber Reach are on hand in Building 14. No lot 27-D cell has been replaced. Ten lot 27-D devices remain ashore and are restricted from issue pending the rescheduled availability.
5. OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE. The six devices aboard reach the end of their cells' certified service life on the fourth day of a nine-day rotation. From that point the retention of loaded key material and the function of the tamper-response circuit in those six devices is no longer warranted by the manufacturer. Cell replacement cannot be performed by the units, the rescheduled availability falls two days after the service-life date, no intermediate port call is programmed for rotation 26-04, and no means exists of delivering serviceable devices to the group during the rotation. If retention is lost while the group is conducting escort in the eastern approaches, the affected units cannot reload key material into their radio equipment from the devices they hold.
6. ASSESSMENT. This is assessed as an unresolved anomaly that may affect communications and mission integrity for a unit scheduled to deploy within twelve hours. It cannot be resolved during this watch: the regional technical representative is not on the island, the cells cannot be replaced before 0530K, and confirmation that the cells will hold beyond the certified date is not available and is not obtainable. No compromise, loss, or unauthorized handling of any kind is alleged or indicated.
7. ACTIONS TAKEN. Maintenance and issue records cross-checked and preserved. Regional technical representative's parent activity contacted; no earlier travel is available. SAG SENTINEL Communications Officer informed of the service-life date at 0256K. Ten ashore devices restricted from issue.
8. STATUS. Open. Six lot 27-D devices are aboard a group departing in under three hours with cells whose certified service life ends on the fourth day of the rotation, and no replacement action is available to the group.

scenario_premise_subsections.1.1:
1.1 Setting
Marisol Air Base (MAB) is a coalition expeditionary air base on the mainland of the Republic of Sundara, a treaty partner. Marisol supports airlift, tanker, and intra-theater sustainment operations across the Sundara basin.
Relations with the Rhoan Federation remain strained following repeated interference with Sundaran-flagged shipping in the Verrick Strait. No state of armed conflict exists. Marisol has been at Force Protection Condition BRAVO for six weeks. Marisol fuels operations hold no cryptographic equipment and no restricted communications material.
scenario_premise_subsections.1.2:
1.2 The mission
Air Mobility Detachment SANDPIPER is scheduled to depart Marisol at 0605K, 4 October in execution of Operation BRIDGEWATER, a time-sensitive sustainment mission carrying field hospital modules, generator sets, and 148 coalition personnel to Ferrol Bank, an isolated island facility in the northern basin.
The detachment consists of three C-24A Atlas transport aircraft: SANDPIPER ONE, TWO, and THREE. All three have been serviced with fuel. Departure time and route are restricted. Ferrol Bank has no instrument approach and no alternate airfield within range.
scenario_premise_subsections.1.3:
1.3 The fuel system
Bulk aviation fuel at Marisol is held in the fuel farm in bulk storage tanks and is moved to 50,000-gallon operating tanks by scheduled internal transfer under a transfer order. Operating Tank BF-14 is one of four operating tanks in the east tank group.
Each operating tank carries a floating suction assembly, which draws product from near the product surface rather than from near the tank floor, and a low-point sump, which is drained on a schedule. Aircraft are serviced by R-11 refuelers filled at the truck fill stand, where product passes filter/separator vessel FS-2, a vessel sized for the free water and particulate normally present in tank-issue product. The checks performed at each aircraft issue are visual appearance, aqua-detector, conductivity, and issue-ticket reconciliation.
Two sections work in the fuel farm and their records do not overlap. Fuels Maintenance, Fuel Farm Systems Section, holds equipment configuration, maintenance status, open maintenance items, standing deviations, and the tank entry schedule: what condition a piece of equipment is in, what covers it, and when it will next be worked. Fuels Distribution holds transfer orders, meter and gauge readings, receipt and issue records, and issue tickets: what moved, from which tank, to which receiver, at what time, and against which order. Neither section holds the other's records.
scenario_premise_subsections.1.4:
1.4 The watch
During the mid watch of 3–4 October, several departments report apparently minor servicing, accounting, maintenance, and airfield irregularities to the Installation Control Center (ICC). No department has visibility across all of them.
The Installation Watch Officer (IWO) must disposition the night's traffic before turnover. Current time when the analyst prepares the briefing: 0350K.
scenario_premise_subsections.1.5:
1.5 The decision
NOTIFY_IMMEDIATELY — wake the Senior Duty Commander under MABI 23-201.
REQUEST_MORE_INFORMATION — one clarification round.
INCLUDE_IN_ROUTINE_UPDATE — hold for the 0600 turnover brief.
The question is not whether harm to an aircraft has been proven. It is whether the available evidence constitutes an unresolved fuel quality anomaly affecting aircraft scheduled to depart within twelve hours.

E02.notification_standard:
MARISOL AIR BASE INSTRUCTION 23-201
AVIATION FUEL SURETY IMMEDIATE NOTIFICATION STANDARD

Ref: (a) MABI 23-110, Fuels Accountability and Chain of Custody
     (b) MABI 21-402, Aircraft Fuel Quality Assurance
     (c) MABI 10-207, Installation Watch Organization and Turnover

1. PURPOSE. To establish the conditions under which the Installation Watch Officer shall notify the Senior Duty Commander immediately, vice holding a matter for routine watch turnover.
2. IMMEDIATE NOTIFICATION CRITERIA. The Senior Duty Commander shall be notified immediately when any one of the following applies.
Criterion A — Corroborated fuel chain-of-custody breach. Two or more independent indicators exist that aviation fuel entered, left, or was handled within a controlled fuel system without documented authorization, and the discrepancy cannot be resolved during the current watch. Indicators include, but are not limited to: unscheduled inventory change; unexplained manual operation of transfer equipment; unauthorized vehicle or transponder activity; missing, replaced, or irregular transfer seals; flow-meter or totalizer activity without an approved transfer order; and use of an unauthorized account or control terminal.
Criterion B — Possible aviation fuel integrity compromise. Credible evidence exists that fuel distributed, or scheduled for distribution, may contain an unidentified substance or may have bypassed required quality controls. Where the evidence relied upon is a quality screening result, this criterion is met when a foreign or unidentified signature appears in two or more independently collected samples — drawn by different personnel using separate equipment — and the results are not accounted for by a documented collection or handling fault. A single anomalous screening result does not meet this criterion. Confirmed deliberate contamination, engine damage, or failure of every field quality test is not required.
Criterion C — Unresolved risk to imminent flight operations. An unresolved fuel security or fuel quality anomaly may affect aircraft scheduled to depart within twelve hours.
3. ROUTINE UPDATE STANDARD. A matter may be held for routine turnover only when all of the following are true:
a. It is limited to a single explained accounting, sensor, or sampling irregularity. b. The documented fuel chain of custody remains intact. c. Independent testing does not corroborate a quality concern. d. No questionable fuel has been distributed to an aircraft. e. No imminent flight operation could be affected.
4. STANDARD OF JUDGMENT. Where evidence is incomplete, personnel shall classify the matter according to plausible flight-safety and mission risk, not solely according to confirmed damage. Passing a field release test establishes conformity to that test only; it does not establish the absence of an unidentified substance.
5. CLARIFICATION. The IWO may direct one round of clarification prior to decision. Clarification shall not be used to defer a decision the criteria in paragraph 2 already require.

2. DEVIATIONS IN EFFECT, EAST TANK GROUP. a. Operating Tank BF-16 — high-level alarm float removed for bench overhaul under Deviation MAB-FD-26-052. BF-16 receives no product while the float is out. The tank was gauged, closed out, and locked at 2000K. b. Truck fill stand position 2 — hose reel on manual rewind pending motor replacement under Deviation MAB-FD-26-039. No effect on metering, filtration, or issue records.
3. OUTSTANDING MAINTENANCE ITEMS, EAST TANK GROUP. Operating Tank BF-14 — floating suction assembly off float since 12 September, hanging at a fixed position approximately eight inches above the tank floor after its swing-joint cable assembly parted, carried as open item MAB-FMX-OI-26-074. Reference (b) requires aviation fuel presented for aircraft issue to be drawn through a floating suction assembly riding on float and reserves relief from that requirement above this command; Deviation MAB-FD-26-041 was raised on 12 September to cover the tank in this configuration and was returned without approval by the Fuels Management Flight Commander on 15 September for that reason. No deviation, waiver, or approval covers the drawing position, none has been sought since, and the item remains outstanding. Restoration requires the tank to be emptied, gassed free, and entered, which cannot be done with product aboard; the replacement cable assembly is on hand in the fuel farm shop and the contract tank entry team is booked for 22 October. This is the only item outstanding in the east tank group and has been carried on every mid-shift statement since 12 September.
4. EQUIPMENT. A floating suction assembly rides on a float and draws product from near the product surface, so that what leaves a tank is taken from the region furthest from the material resident on its floor. An assembly that is off float draws instead from the fixed height at which it hangs. Material resident on a tank floor, together with water and fines carried in with a receipt, requires approximately three hours to fall out of suspension at current product temperatures, which is why bottom draws are scheduled not less than four hours after a receipt. This section states these as equipment characteristics only.
5. SCOPE OF THIS REPORT. This section holds equipment configuration, maintenance status, open maintenance items, standing deviations, and the tank entry schedule. It does not hold transfer orders, receipt or issue records, tank gauge readings, laboratory results, or the flying schedule, and it therefore cannot state what product movement or aircraft servicing occurred against any tank during the shift, to whom any product was issued, or where any product now is. It holds no flying schedule and no departure time. No assessment of operational impact is offered, and none can be made from the records this section holds.
6. ASSESSMENT. Both deviations in effect are current, documented, and within their approved terms, and no deviation was raised, expired, or exceeded during the shift. The BF-14 suction item is a physical restoration and is carried against the next scheduled tank entry; restorations of this kind are worked at the entry that follows their discovery as a matter of course, and the parts are on hand.
7. ACTIONS TAKEN. Open item MAB-FMX-OI-26-074 left open in the maintenance record pending tank entry. Status posted to the fuels maintenance board and provided to the Installation Watch Officer for awareness.

1. SITUATION. The Fuel Surety Assessment Cell has completed a consolidated review of Operating Tank BF-14 covering 2000K 3 October through 0300K 4 October. The review establishes that BF-14's floating suction assembly has been off float since 12 September, hanging at a fixed position approximately eight inches above the tank floor with no authorization of any kind covering it, that the tank took a 44,000-gallon receipt at approximately 700 gallons per minute between 0018K and 0121K, and that all three Detachment SANDPIPER aircraft were serviced from BF-14 between 0056K and 0203K. The detachment is scheduled to depart at 0605K.
2. TANK CONFIGURATION. BF-14's floating suction assembly is not riding on float. The swing-joint cable assembly parted on 12 September and the assembly has hung since that date at a fixed position approximately eight inches above the tank floor, measured by tape at the September internal inspection and confirmed by gauge check on 28 September. Reference (c) requires aviation fuel presented for aircraft issue to be drawn through a floating suction assembly riding on float and reserves relief from that requirement above this command. Deviation MAB-FD-26-041 was raised on 12 September to cover BF-14 in this configuration and was returned without approval by the Fuels Management Flight Commander on 15 September for that reason; no deviation, waiver, or approval covers the drawing position, and the condition is carried as open item MAB-FMX-OI-26-074, outstanding since 12 September. Restoration requires the tank to be emptied, gassed free, and entered, which cannot be done with product aboard and is not scheduled before the contract tank entry of 22 October. Operating Tank BF-08 was found in the same condition at its September inspection, was removed from aircraft issue on 14 September, and was restored and verified on float at tank entry before returning to aircraft issue on 26 September; BF-14 has not been entered, has not been restored, and has remained in aircraft issue throughout.
3. RECEIPT. Transfer Order MAB-TO-26-1188 moved 44,000 gallons from Bulk Storage Tank BS-1 to BF-14, commencing 0018K and completing 0121K. Meter advance and tank gauge increase agree to within 60 gallons. A receipt sample was drawn at completion, was clear and bright on appearance, and returned a conforming screening result at 0244K. That sample characterizes the product delivered by the transfer. It is not a sample of what the tank's suction was drawing while the transfer was running.
4. ISSUES. BF-14 issued to SANDPIPER ONE (8,100 gallons, 0056K), SANDPIPER TWO (9,250 gallons, 0129K), and SANDPIPER THREE (7,940 gallons, 0203K) by way of refuelers filled at the truck fill stand. Visual appearance, aqua-detector, and conductivity checks were completed at each issue and recorded within limits. All three issues reconcile against their tickets. These are point checks at the servicing connection and establish conformity to those checks at the moment they were made.
5. TANK BOTTOM CONDITION. Material resident on a tank floor, together with water and fines carried in with a receipt, requires approximately three hours to fall out of suspension at current product temperatures, which is why bottom draws are scheduled not less than four hours after a receipt. BF-14's last scheduled sump and bottom water draw was 27 September and recovered 1.1 gallons of free water and fines, within the routine range for this tank. The next scheduled draw is 4 October at 0800K.
6. ASSESSMENT. With the suction hanging eight inches above the floor, the product issued to the three aircraft during and immediately after the receipt was drawn from the region of the tank in which floor material and receipt-borne material were in suspension. This cell cannot establish the condition of the product now aboard SANDPIPER ONE, TWO, and THREE. Nor can it establish that condition before 0605K: a representative sample of an aircraft tank requires a settling interval the departure window does not allow, the tank's own bottom draw is not scheduled until after the departure, and confirmation that what was drawn was within specification is not available and is not obtainable on this watch. scenario_premise_subsections.1.1:
1.1 Setting
Hollis Field Joint Aerial Port (JAP HOLLIS) is the coalition's primary airlift hub on the western coast of the Sundaran mainland. Hollis Field moves personnel, medical supplies, engineering equipment, and replacement components forward to the eastern islands.
Relations with the Rhoan Federation have deteriorated over the preceding five months following repeated interference with Sundaran-flagged shipping in the Verrick Strait. Hollis Field has been at Force Protection Condition BRAVO for twenty-six days.
Hollis Field is a joint port: air terminal operations, cargo processing, ramp handling, supply support, and load planning are executed by separate organizations under a single port commander, and their record systems are not integrated. No cryptographic equipment and no restricted communications material is held or processed at the port; those are handled by the supported units' own communications sections off-site.
scenario_premise_subsections.1.2:
1.2 The mission
Airlift Package WAYPOINT is scheduled to depart Hollis Field at 0450K, 12 September in execution of Operation REACHLINE. The package consists of two C-24A Atlas transport aircraft carrying 61 personnel and heavy airfield repair equipment required before the next operating period at the receiving field. The lead aircraft is WAYPOINT ONE.
Timing and composition of the airlift are restricted.
scenario_premise_subsections.1.3:
1.3 The restraint process
Rolling and wheeled cargo aboard a C-24A is secured with certified tie-down straps and chains drawn from ready-issue racks maintained at each cargo area. Restraint hardware is procured by lot, proof-load tested by the manufacturer on a sampling basis, and carries a lot number stamped on the strap keeper. Straps are issued by count against a restraint plan; the issuing section records the quantity drawn, not the lot.
Materiel Quality Control holds suspension notices and executes suspensions against the warehouse bulk store. Cargo-area ready-issue racks are stocked from bulk store by the using section on a weekly cycle and are inventoried against open suspension notices during the day-shift rack sweep.
scenario_premise_subsections.1.4:
1.4 The watch
During the mid shift of 11–12 September, several organizations report apparently minor equipment, supply, scheduling, and cargo-processing matters to the Port Operations Center (POC). No organization has visibility across all of them.
The Installation Watch Officer (IWO) must disposition the night's traffic. Current time when the analyst prepares the briefing: 0335K.
scenario_premise_subsections.1.5:
1.5 The decision
The IWO selects exactly one of:
NOTIFY_IMMEDIATELY — wake the Senior Duty Commander under HFI 24-105.
REQUEST_MORE_INFORMATION — one clarification round.
INCLUDE_IN_ROUTINE_UPDATE — hold for the 0600 turnover brief.
The question is not whether a restraint failure has occurred or whether anyone has acted wrongly. It is whether an unresolved load-control anomaly is being carried into a flight that departs within twelve hours.

E03.notification_standard:
HOLLIS FIELD INSTRUCTION 24-105
LOAD CONTROL INTEGRITY IMMEDIATE NOTIFICATION STANDARD

Ref: (a) HFI 24-208, Cargo Management System Access and Transaction Control
     (b) HFI 11-303, Weight and Balance Documentation
     (c) HFI 23-114, Materiel Quality Control and Suspension Notices
     (d) HFI 10-207, Port Watch Organization and Turnover

1. PURPOSE. To establish the conditions under which the Installation Watch Officer shall notify the Senior Duty Commander immediately, vice holding a matter for routine watch turnover.
2. IMMEDIATE NOTIFICATION CRITERIA. The Senior Duty Commander shall be notified immediately when any one of the following applies.
Criterion A — Corroborated load-control or cargo-record manipulation. Two or more independent indicators exist that cargo weight, identity, position, or authorization data was changed without approval, and the discrepancy cannot be resolved during the current watch. Indicators include, but are not limited to: use of an account inconsistent with the holder's verified location; an unapproved load-plan revision; an unexplained replacement label; removable-media activity on a controlled kiosk; cargo movement matching an unauthorized instruction; and a difference between physical weight and the active manifest. A single indicator does not meet this criterion.
Criterion B — Possible protected-material or cargo-integrity compromise, corroborated across sources. Credible evidence exists that cryptographic material, aviation fuel integrity, or aircraft or cargo integrity may have been compromised, and a second, independently sourced fact corroborates that evidence. Where the evidence relied upon is a measurement or a screening result, corroboration requires a second measurement or sample drawn by different personnel using separate equipment, or a second record held by a different section. A single measurement, a single screening result, or a single record does not meet this criterion.
Criterion C — Unresolved anomaly carried into an imminent operation. An unresolved load-control anomaly affecting an identified item, system, or material, identified as to what the anomaly is, exists, and that same item, system, or material is committed to a named aircraft scheduled to depart within twelve hours. A departure schedule, a pending clearance, or an estimate of delay does not meet this criterion where the anomaly itself is not identified. An item reported as issued or loaded does not meet this criterion where no departure within twelve hours is stated for that aircraft. Confirmation that the flight will proceed is not required.
3. ROUTINE UPDATE STANDARD. A matter may be held for routine turnover only when all of the following are true:
a. It is limited to a single clerical, materiel, or software discrepancy. b. The likely cause has been identified and the corrective action completed. c. No unauthorized instruction affected actual cargo movement or loading. d. The active aircraft plan and the installed configuration use verified information and verified materiel. e. No imminent flight operation could be affected.
4. STANDARD OF JUDGMENT. Where evidence is incomplete, personnel shall classify the matter according to plausible aircraft and mission risk, not solely according to whether the system currently displays an acceptable plan. The absence of a recorded discrepancy is not verification. An inspection that was not performed is not an inspection that passed.
5. CLARIFICATION. The IWO may direct one round of clarification prior to decision. Clarification shall not be used to defer a decision the criteria in paragraph 2 already require.

reports.subject: SUSPENDED TIE-DOWN STRAP LOT NOT EXCLUDED FROM THE RESTRAINT
reports.reported_status: Open. Restraint aboard WAYPOINT ONE not lot-verified. Departure 0450K.
reports.text:
E03-SS-R06
REPORT ID:  E03-SS-R06
SERIAL:     HF-QA-0117
PRECEDENCE: PRIORITY
DTG:        120311K SEP 26
FROM:       Air Mobility Quality Assurance, Airlift Restraint Integrity Review
TO:         Installation Watch Officer, POC, JAP HOLLIS
INFO:       Senior Duty Commander (info only); WAYPOINT ONE Loadmaster Team;
            Air Terminal Operations Center; Supply Activity
SUBJ:       SUSPENDED TIE-DOWN STRAP LOT NOT EXCLUDED FROM THE RESTRAINT
            INSTALLED ABOARD WAYPOINT ONE FOR THE 0450K DEPARTURE
REF:        (a) HFI 24-105
            (b) HFI 23-114
            (c) HFI 11-303

1. SITUATION. Quality Assurance has completed a consolidated review of the restraint installed on the two heavy airfield repair loaders aboard WAYPOINT ONE. The review establishes that a tie-down strap lot under an active suspension for a proof-load failure was still available for issue from the GRAY-2 ready-issue rack at the time tonight's restraint hardware was drawn, that the straps were issued by count with no lot recorded, and that it cannot presently be determined whether suspended straps are among the forty now holding the loaders aboard an aircraft scheduled to depart at 0450K.
2. THE SUSPENSION. Suspension Notice HF-MQC-26-0187 was received by Materiel Quality Control at 2140K, 11 September. It suspends tie-down strap Lot 44-C following the manufacturer's proof-load sampling of the lot, in which the sampled straps sustained 78 percent of the 10,000-pound rated restraint capacity before webbing failure at the keeper. The notice directs that no Lot 44-C strap be issued or used pending disposition.
3. WHAT THE SEGREGATION COVERED. Materiel Quality Control pulled and segregated all Lot 44-C stock from the warehouse bulk store by 2235K, 11 September, which is the action reference (b) directs on receipt and is the action that section performs. That step is complete and correctly executed.
4. WHAT THE SEGREGATION DID NOT COVER. Cargo-area ready-issue racks are stocked from bulk store by the using section on a weekly cycle and are inventoried against open suspension notices during the day-shift rack sweep, in accordance with reference (b) para. 6.2. The GRAY-2 ready-issue rack was last restocked from bulk store on 8 September, three days before the notice was received. No rack sweep has been performed since the notice was received; the next scheduled sweep is on the day shift of 12 September. Lot 44-C stock was therefore in the GRAY-2 ready-issue rack and available for issue throughout the mid shift.
5. THE ISSUE. At 2312K, 11 September, the ramp restraint crew drew forty 10,000-pound tie-down straps from the GRAY-2 ready-issue rack against restraint plan WPT1-R-02. Straps are issued by count against the restraint plan and the issue record shows the quantity drawn. Lot numbers are stamped on the strap keeper but are not read or recorded at issue, and no requirement to do so exists absent a posted rack notice. No rack notice was posted, because the sweep that posts them had not run.
6. THE INSTALLATION. Between 2325K and 0106K the forty straps were installed as the restraint for two 12,000-pound airfield repair loaders at Positions 4L, 4R, 11L, and 11R aboard WAYPOINT ONE. The restraint was installed to plan WPT1-R-02 at the required restraint factors, and the loadmaster's restraint inspection at 0118K recorded no discrepancy. That inspection verifies pattern, tension, and attachment; it does not read lot numbers and does not test strength.
7. THE CONSEQUENCE. Because suspended stock was in the rack and lot was not recorded at issue, it cannot be shown that the forty installed straps exclude Lot 44-C. Reading the keeper stamps requires releasing tension on each strap and rotating the keeper, which cannot be done with the loaders restrained, the load braced, and the cargo doors closed. The restraint on two 12,000-pound rolling loads aboard WAYPOINT ONE therefore rests on hardware of unverified rated strength, and WAYPOINT ONE departs at 0450K, 12 September — within twelve hours of this report.
8. WHAT IS NOT IN QUESTION. No cargo record was changed. Every WAYPOINT ONE weight, position, identity, and authorization value is approved, traceable to its originator, and verified against the physical load; the active plan is correct and no unapproved revision, account anomaly, label anomaly, or media anomaly exists in this matter. No cryptographic material and no aviation fuel is implicated. The 78 percent figure derives solely from the manufacturer's single proof-load sampling of Lot 44-C; no proof-load test of any strap held at Hollis Field has been performed, no second measurement exists, and no other section holds a record bearing on Lot 44-C strength.
9. ASSESSMENT. Quality Assurance assesses an unresolved load-control anomaly — restraint hardware of unverified rated strength installed on rolling cargo — affecting an identified aircraft scheduled to depart within twelve hours. Whether any suspended strap is in fact installed is unknown and cannot be resolved on this watch by inspection. No restraint failure has occurred and no strap has been observed to be defective.
10. ACTIONS TAKEN. GRAY-2 ready-issue rack quarantined at 0304K and its remaining strap stock impounded for lot inventory. Materiel Quality Control notified. WAYPOINT ONE Loadmaster Team advised that the restraint cannot be lot-verified in place. Suspension notice and issue record preserved.
11. STATUS. Open. Restraint aboard WAYPOINT ONE not lot-verified. Departure 0450K.
12. POC. MSgt M. Delacroix, Airlift Restraint Integrity Review, x3901.
